role_summary: Leads Turing's forward-deployed engineering operation — the team that goes into Fortune 500 clients and builds/deploys GenAI systems on-site. Equal parts technical architect and delivery leader. Must be hands-on enough to drive architectural decisions and senior enough to hold the room with a CIO. Not a research role, not a pure management role, not a strategy role. Applied GenAI delivery across regulated verticals (BFSI priority, plus life sciences, retail/CPG). The person who turns Turing's AI capabilities into repeatable, deployed reality inside complex enterprises.
role_evolution_note: This role has been in flux. Originally scoped as 'Head of Applied AI Lab' with a pure BFSI focus. Now repositioned as Head of Forward Deployed Engineering with multi-vertical scope. The JD still reflects the older framing. Evaluate candidates against THIS brief, not the posted JD.

capability_areas.name: Enterprise GenAI Delivery
capability_areas.description: Has personally architected and deployed GenAI systems in production enterprise environments. Not demos, not POCs that died, not strategy decks — systems that went live and stayed live. RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, copilots, orchestration frameworks, evaluation systems.
builder_signals: Specific tools named: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, DSPy, Haystack, CrewAI, Temporal, etc.
Phrases: 'I architected', 'I built', 'I deployed to production', 'I designed the evaluation framework'
Production deployment evidence: uptime, scale, user counts, latency requirements
GitHub/open source contributions in GenAI tooling
Fine-tuned models, built RAG pipelines, designed agentic architectures THEMSELVES
user_signals: Led team that built (managed, not built personally)
Adopted GitHub Copilot / Devin / off-the-shelf AI tools
AI transformation officer / AI strategy lead framing

capability_areas.name: Forward-Deployed / Client-Facing Engineering Leadership
capability_areas.description: Has led engineering teams that deploy directly into client environments — not building internal product, but delivering custom technical solutions on-site or embedded with external clients. Understands the operational mode: scoping with clients, adapting architecture to client constraints, managing delivery timelines against client expectations, building trust through technical credibility.
builder_signals: Led engineering teams embedded at client sites
Personally scoped and delivered technical solutions for external clients
Managed multi-client delivery portfolio
Built repeatable delivery playbooks from client engagements
Experience at: enterprise AI startups, consulting firms with real engineering (not just strategy), or tech companies with professional services arms
user_signals: Pure pre-sales / solutions architecture (demos, not delivery)

capability_areas.name: Vertical Domain Fluency
capability_areas.description: Has built AI systems that operated within the constraints of regulated or complex enterprise environments. The signal is NOT 'worked at Goldman' — it's 'built systems that had to satisfy compliance, audit, data governance, and regulatory requirements in a vertical context.' BFSI is the priority vertical, but life sciences and retail/CPG experience also qualifies.
builder_signals: Built AI for financial services clients (from outside: deployed INTO banks, not just worked AT banks)
Built AI under regulatory constraints: SOX, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, FDA, GDPR applied to sensitive data
Deployed AI in environments with audit trail / explainability requirements
Experience with data governance in regulated contexts (data residency, PII handling, model governance)
Worked at a tech company that SELLS INTO regulated verticals (Palantir, Dataiku, C3.ai, enterprise AI consultancies)
user_signals: Worked at a bank but in a non-technical capacity
Managed a data team at a pharma company (management, not building)
Vertical experience is entirely in unregulated tech (ad-tech, social media, gaming)
capability_areas.vertical_note: BFSI is highest priority but not a hard gate. A candidate with deep life sciences + GenAI delivery experience is a strong fit. A candidate with zero regulated-vertical experience is a weak fit regardless of technical depth.

capability_areas.name: Delivery Infrastructure & Playbook Building
capability_areas.description: Has built the systems and processes that make client delivery repeatable — not just doing it once, but creating the scaffolding so a team can do it at scale. Reusable architectures, delivery playbooks, quality standards, team scaling frameworks. This is what separates a senior IC who delivers well from a leader who builds a delivery organization.
builder_signals: Built reusable GenAI reference architectures used across multiple clients
Created delivery playbooks / methodologies adopted by teams
Scaled an engineering delivery org from small to large
Established engineering standards and quality processes for client delivery
Built internal platforms/tools that accelerated client deployments
user_signals: Only ever delivered bespoke solutions (no repeatability)
Managed delivery but didn't build the operational infrastructure
Strategy consulting on 'how to build a practice' without actually building one

minimum_bar.experience_note: 12yr floor. Must have substantial post-IC delivery leadership. A 12yr person who's been leading client-facing engineering teams for 4+ years qualifies. A 12yr IC with no delivery leadership doesn't.
minimum_bar.title_ceiling: Executive Director at a major bank is the max. In tech terms: VP at a large company is context-dependent (okay if hands-on, skip if pure management). SVP, C-suite at large org, MD, Partner at Big4 = too senior.
minimum_bar.title_floor: Senior Engineering Manager, Principal Engineer (with client delivery evidence). Staff Engineer with no delivery leadership = too junior for the role.
minimum_bar.technical_depth: Must show direct, personal involvement in BUILDING GenAI systems. Not managing a team that builds, not selling it, not developing strategy around it. The test: could this person whiteboard a RAG architecture and defend their design choices?
minimum_bar.genai_recency: Post-2022 GenAI work required. Pre-LLM ML experience is valuable context but insufficient alone. Must show evidence of working with LLMs, not just classical ML.
minimum_bar.location: Must be NYC metro. No exceptions, no relocation candidates.

employer_context_preference.rule: Prioritize candidates from tech companies that SERVE regulated verticals over candidates FROM regulated vertical institutions. This is a preference, not a gate.
employer_context_preference.tier_1_prefer: Enterprise AI companies, AI consulting with real engineering, tech companies with professional services / forward-deployed teams, applied AI startups selling into regulated industries
employer_context_preference.tier_2_accept: Regulated vertical institutions (banks, pharma, insurers) where the candidate was clearly a BUILDER — hands-on engineering leader, not just a manager or strategist. The test: did they build the system or manage the people who built it?
employer_context_preference.tier_3_weaker: Regulated vertical institutions where the candidate's role was management/strategy layer over engineering. Not auto-skip, but needs very strong Gate 3 evidence to compensate.
employer_context_preference.tier_4_skip_unless_exceptional: Cloud vendor solutions architects, Big4 consulting partners, large-org C-suite, pure internal product companies with no client-facing delivery

preview_scan_criteria.rule: Before opening any profile, triage from the preview snippet using these four signals. If two or more are failing, skip without opening.
signals: TITLE — Must be Director, Senior Director, Head of, Principal (with leadership context), VP at growth-stage company, or Engineering Manager at a company known for strong EM scope. SVP/MD/Partner/CXO at large org = skip. Pure IC titles (Staff Engineer, Senior Engineer) without leadership context = skip.

COMPANY CONTEXT — Look for tech companies, AI companies, consulting firms with engineering practices, or enterprise software companies. Career spent entirely at one legacy bank/pharma/retailer with no tech-side experience = weaker signal. NOT a hard skip — but flag for careful Gate 3 review.
YEARS — Must show 12+ years visible experience. If LinkedIn preview shows <12yr total career, skip.

HEADER KEYWORDS — Builder language: GenAI, LLM, RAG, agentic, applied AI, ML engineering, AI delivery, forward-deployed, solutions engineering, technical delivery. Red flags that justify skip without opening: AI Strategy, AI Transformation, Product Manager, Customer Success, Pre-Sales, Solutions Architect at cloud vendor, Fractional CTO.

hard_skips: Zero post-2022 GenAI work evidence across entire profile
Pure researcher with no production deployment or client delivery experience
Fresh grad, bootcamp, or early-career profile
Annotation/data labeling worker (Scale AI, Outlier, Appen)
IT auditor, QA tester, project manager with no engineering crossover
Solo fractional executive / 1-person boutique consultant with no team leadership evidence

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Solutions Architect at cloud vendor (AWS, Azure, GCP)
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Customer-facing pre-sales and demos, not production AI engineering delivery. They show products, they don't build systems.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Head of AI Products / VP AI Products / Product Manager of AI
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Product management layer over engineering. Directs engineering, does not build. Even if at a regulated vertical firm.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: AI Transformation Executive / Chief AI Officer at large org / AI Strategy Lead
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Strategy and transformation framing without implementation evidence. The higher the title at a large org, the further from building.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: C-suite at large org (CTO 400+ person eng org, CDAO, CIO, EVP, SVP, MD at major bank)
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Too senior. Scope and comp ceiling mismatch. The role needs someone who still gets their hands dirty.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Partner at Big4 consulting (Deloitte, Accenture, McKinsey, EY, PwC, KPMG)
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Too senior, wrong operational mode (advisory, not delivery engineering).

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: AI experience = adopting tools, not building systems
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Implementing GitHub Copilot, Devin, or off-the-shelf AI tools is not building AI systems. Rolling out an LLM vendor's API to internal users is not GenAI delivery.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Customer Success or Pre-Sales adjacent role
clear_skips_from_review.reason: Client-facing adoption and demos, not engineering delivery.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Pure internal product engineer with zero client-facing delivery experience
clear_skips_from_review.reason: The role requires client-facing delivery leadership. Brilliant engineers who've only built internal products will struggle with the client-facing dimension. Not a hard skip but a serious yellow flag.

clear_skips_from_review.pattern: Career entirely in unregulated tech verticals (ad-tech, social media, gaming, consumer SaaS)
clear_skips_from_review.reason: No exposure to the regulatory/compliance/governance constraints that define delivery in BFSI, life sciences, or retail/CPG. Not auto-skip, but needs very compelling GenAI depth to compensate.

gate_evaluation_order.name: Diversity (first pass only)
gate_evaluation_order.rule: Women OR non-Indian candidates only on diversity pass. South Asian males = skip without opening.

gate_evaluation_order.name: Seniority calibration
gate_evaluation_order.rule: ED at major bank equivalent is the ceiling. In tech: Director to Senior Director sweet spot, VP at growth company okay, VP at large company context-dependent. Below: Senior EM or Principal with delivery leadership evidence. Above: SVP/MD/Partner/C-suite at large org = too senior.

gate_evaluation_order.name: Technical depth (hard filter)
gate_evaluation_order.rule: The whiteboard test: could this person diagram a production GenAI architecture and defend their design choices? Look for builder evidence, not management evidence.
pass_signals: Specific GenAI tools personally used: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, DSPy, Haystack, CrewAI, Temporal
Action verbs: 'I architected', 'I implemented', 'I built', 'I deployed to production'
Production deployment specifics: scale, latency, uptime, user counts
GitHub contributions, technical blog posts, conference talks with code
Fine-tuned models, built RAG pipelines, designed evaluation frameworks THEMSELVES
fail_signals: All evidence is management/strategy: 'led team of', 'drove strategy for', 'oversaw development of'
AI experience limited to tool adoption (Copilot, Devin rollout)
AI Transformation / AI Strategy titles without implementation evidence

gate_evaluation_order.name: Client-facing delivery experience
gate_evaluation_order.rule: Must show evidence of leading engineering delivery FOR external clients — not internal product development. Professional services, consulting engineering, forward-deployed engineering, enterprise implementation, solutions delivery. Candidates who've only built internal products need extremely compelling evidence on all other gates to compensate.
pass_signals: Led engineering teams embedded at client sites
Managed delivery against client timelines and requirements
Experience at consulting firms, professional services orgs, or enterprise AI companies with client delivery models
Built and sold technical solutions to enterprise clients
soft_pass: Internal engineering leader who worked closely with clients on integration/customization
Product engineering leader at a B2B company with deep customer engineering involvement

gate_evaluation_order.name: Vertical domain fluency
gate_evaluation_order.rule: At least one regulated vertical: BFSI (priority), life sciences, or retail/CPG. The evidence can be from the TECH side (deployed AI into banks) or the VERTICAL side (built AI at a bank). No regulated vertical exposure at all = weak fit.
gate_evaluation_order.note: The signal is 'built AI that operated under vertical constraints' — not 'worked at a company in that vertical.'

archetypes: Director of AI/Engineering at an enterprise AI company (Palantir, Dataiku, C3.ai, Scale AI enterprise side, etc.) who's spent 5+ years deploying GenAI into BFSI or life sciences clients. Has both the technical depth and the client-facing muscle.

Head of Engineering at an applied AI startup (<200 people) building GenAI products for regulated industries. Personally architects solutions and leads client delivery. Previously held a senior technical role at a bank or pharma company where they built (not managed) AI systems.

Senior Director / Engineering Director at a consulting firm's AI engineering practice (not advisory — actual build/deploy) serving Fortune 500 clients. Deloitte/Accenture tech side (not partner level), boutique AI consulting firms, Big4 tech delivery arms.

VP or Head of AI at a fintech / health-tech / retail-tech company that sells into regulated enterprises. Leads a team of 15-50 engineers, still reviews PRs, personally drives architecture decisions for key clients.

non_fit_patterns.pattern: Career bank lifer — 20 years at one major bank, rose through management ranks
non_fit_patterns.reason: Likely too embedded in one institution's culture and processes. May struggle with the multi-client, startup-speed operational mode. Not auto-skip — but needs very strong builder and GenAI evidence.
No delivery experience, no client-facing muscle. Even with strong GenAI depth, missing the operational dimension.

non_fit_patterns.pattern: Enterprise sales / business development disguised as technical leadership
non_fit_patterns.reason: Titles like 'VP of Client Solutions' or 'Head of Strategic Partnerships' — client-facing but not engineering.

non_fit_patterns.pattern: Large-org middle manager who's been 'overseeing AI initiatives'
non_fit_patterns.reason: Overseeing ≠ building. The verb choice matters. 'Oversaw the development of our AI platform' vs 'Built our RAG pipeline and deployed it to 3 production clients' — only the second one passes Gate 3.

diversity_mandate.skip_rule: South Asian males = skip without opening on first pass
diversity_mandate.note: Finding 3-5 diverse candidates who meet this bar across a full search run is a successful diversity pass.

market_density_note: The intersection of NYC + 12yr+ + GenAI builder + client-facing delivery + regulated vertical is narrow. Expect high noise-to-signal. Dragnet or titration architecture recommended — cast wide on GenAI delivery language, let the gates do the precision work.
search_kit_note: The existing Head of AI Lab kit was BFSI-anchored. Will likely need regeneration for the FDE framing. Use it if available but don't expect it to fully cover life sciences and retail/CPG vocabulary.
linkedin_project_note: Project name reflects the old role title. Do not rename — existing saves are in this project.

permanent_filters.company_filters: NONE — do not anchor on company names
permanent_filters.keywords: Boolean strings from search kit, adapted for multi-vertical scope

execution_notes: This brief deliberately avoids company-name anchoring. Do NOT use company names as search filters — use capability signals.
Vertical filtering happens at evaluation time (Gate 5), not search time. Search strings should target GenAI delivery capability, not vertical-specific vocabulary.
Expect high noise on broad Recall strings — the five gates are the precision levers, not the search strings.
The employer_context_preference tiers should inform evaluation confidence, not search filtering. A Tier 1 candidate with moderate evidence > a Tier 3 candidate with strong evidence.
Minimum 5 pages per string before marking complete
Do NOT remove any candidates already saved to the LinkedIn project
